prompt: We're replacing our cron-based notification system with a new fanout service. The team has written up a design - it's in docs/design/notification-fanout.md, with supporting context in the docs/ and data/ folders. I need you to review it and write up what you find. We've had issues with duplicate sends before (see the incident report), and costs are tight. Look for things that could break in production, cost surprises, or compliance gaps. Write your review to REVIEW.md at the top of the project. End it with a fenced json list of findings, each with location (the section number of the document, like 3.2), severity (critical, high, medium, low or nit), issue and fix.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const S=["critical","high","medium","low","nit"];process.exit(L.every(x=>x.location&&S.includes(String(x.severity).toLowerCase())&&(x.issue||x.fix||x.text))?0:1)'

node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const H=new Set();for(const l of fs.readFileSync("docs/design/notification-fanout.md","utf8").split("\n")){const m=l.match(/^#+\s*(?:section\s*)?(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)/i);if(m)H.add(m[1])}process.exit(L.every(x=>{const m=String(x.location).match(/\d+(?:\.\d+)*/);return m&&H.has(m[0])})?0:1)'

rubric.criterion: Each important finding explains the concrete consequence in this project and proposes a fix a developer can act on, without inventing problems that aren't there (code cannot check this because it requires understanding technical tradeoffs and project context).

findingsKey.finding: Consumers lack deduplication mechanism, which combined with at-least-once delivery will cause duplicate notifications as documented in the January incident report.
Retry logic has no cap and no dead-letter queue, meaning vendor outages could create infinite retry storms that overwhelm the system.
Design capacity of 10,000 notifications/sec is 20x the current peak of 500/sec shown in traffic-by-hour.csv, with no justification for such over-provisioning.
SendGrid limit is 100 emails/sec per vendor-limits.yaml, but the design doesn't include throttling mechanisms to prevent exceeding this limit.
User contact data (device tokens, email addresses) is included in each queued event and stored for 30 days without encryption, violating data protection requirements in service-targets.md.
99.95% availability target requires multi-zone deployment, but the design specifies single availability zone in us-east-1.
Quiet hours implementation uses hardcoded US/Eastern timezone instead of respecting individual user time zones and preferences.

verdicts.note: Prompt gives general categories (breakage, cost, compliance) but doesn't name specific issues, number of problems, or review methods. Mention of past duplicate incidents is reasonable context.
Clear: review docs/design/notification-fanout.md and supporting docs, write to REVIEW.md, output as fenced JSON with section, severity, issue, fix.
Several items require cross-file analysis (capacity vs traffic CSV, rate limits vs vendor limits, encryption requirement vs design). Quick review wouldn't find all items.

All 7 key items have evidence in fixture: deduplication (5.3 no duplicate detection), retry (5.3 indefinite, no DLQ), capacity (5.5 10k vs traffic 550), throttling (5.4.2 100/sec limit no throttling), PII (5.7.1 not encrypted vs service-targets encryption required), zone (5.6 single AZ for 99.95%), timezone (5.8 fixed US/Eastern). All severities reasonable.
File names are appropriate supporting docs (incident report, vendor limits, traffic data). No inline hints or comments in design document pointing at problems.
